# youtrack_mail_rule (Resource)

Manages a mail rule of the YouTrack mailbox integration: which emails of a mailbox (`youtrack_mailbox`) YouTrack turns into issues and comments of a project, and how.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "support_mailbox_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "youtrack_project" "support" {
  name         = "Support"
  short_name   = "SUP"
  leader_login = "john.doe"
}

resource "youtrack_mailbox" "support" {
  protocol = "IMAPS"
  host     = "imap.example.com"
  port     = 993
  login    = "support@example.com"
  password = var.support_mailbox_password
}

# Turn the emails sent to support@example.com into issues of the Support project,
# with the sender as reporter, ignoring newsletters.
resource "youtrack_mail_rule" "support" {
  mailbox_id        = youtrack_mailbox.support.id
  project_id        = youtrack_project.support.id
  maintainer_login  = "john.doe"
  to                = "support@example.com"
  spam_filter_mode  = "BLOCK_TICKETS"
  new_issue_command = "Type Support"

  filters = [
    {
      scope          = "SUBJECT"
      patterns       = ["newsletter", "unsubscribe"]
      accept_matched = false
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mailbox_id` (String) ID of the mailbox the rule reads emails from. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `maintainer_login` (String) Login of the user YouTrack notifies when it cannot process an email.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the rule creates issues in.

### Optional

- `default_reporter_login` (String) Login of the predefined reporter. Required for `SENDER_OR_DEFAULT` and `ALWAYS_PREDEFINED`, not allowed otherwise.
- `delete_after_fetch` (Boolean) Whether to delete emails from the mailbox once processed. Defaults to false.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is disabled. Defaults to false.
- `do_not_discard_brackets_contents` (Boolean) Whether to keep the text in square brackets of the subject in the issue summary. Defaults to false.
- `fetch_old_emails` (Boolean) Whether to process emails that were already in the mailbox, including read ones. Defaults to false.
- `filter_auto_replies` (Boolean) Whether to ignore automatic replies, such as out-of-office messages. Defaults to true.
- `filters` (Attributes List) Filters that accept or reject emails by their subject or body. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))
- `folder` (String) Mailbox folder to read emails from. When unset, YouTrack reads the inbox.
- `new_comment_command` (String) Command applied to the issue of every comment the rule creates.
- `new_issue_command` (String) Command applied to every issue the rule creates, such as `Type Bug`.
- `original_timestamps` (Boolean) Whether issues and comments get the date of the email instead of the date it was processed. Defaults to true.
- `plain_text_description` (Boolean) Whether to use the plain text part of the email as issue description instead of the HTML part. Defaults to false.
- `reply_to` (String) Reply-To address of the notifications YouTrack sends about the issues this rule creates.
- `reporter_policy` (String) Who becomes the reporter of an issue created from an email: `SENDER_OR_NEW_USER` (the sender, registered as a new user if unknown), `SENDER_OR_DEFAULT` (the sender, or `default_reporter_login` if unknown) or `ALWAYS_PREDEFINED` (always `default_reporter_login`). Defaults to `SENDER_OR_NEW_USER`.
- `spam_filter_mode` (String) What to do with emails the spam filter flags: `NONE` (ignore the spam filter), `MARK_TICKETS` (create the issue and mark it as spam) or `BLOCK_TICKETS` (drop the email). Defaults to `MARK_TICKETS`.
- `to` (String) Only process emails sent to this address.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Mail rule ID.

<a id="nestedatt--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters`

Required:

- `accept_matched` (Boolean) true to process only the emails that match, false to reject the emails that match.
- `patterns` (List of String) Patterns to match.
- `scope` (String) What the patterns are matched against: `SUBJECT`, `BODY` or `SUBJECT_AND_BODY`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/sh
# Import a mail rule by its ID.
terraform import youtrack_mail_rule.support 416-0
```
